channel.title: SecuBuzz · Cybersecurity News Briefs
channel.description: Fast, factual 60-word cybersecurity briefs and CISA KEV alerts for security professionals.

item.title: GL.iNet Cloud Flaw Enables Router and KVM Malware
item.description: Hackers leveraged a flaw in GL.iNet’s cloud-based remote-management service to compromise customer routers and KVM devices. The vulnerability permits unauthenticated code execution, enabling attackers to drop custom malware, establish backdoors, and spawn reverse shells for persistent remote control. GL.iNet has released a patch for the cloud service; administrators should apply the update immediately and verify device firmware integrity.

item.title: Debian, Ubuntu Remove rsyslogd Timestamp Config Directive
item.description: Debian and Ubuntu removed a configuration directive from rsyslogd in early 2023, changing syslog timestamp handling. The change removes a legacy option that allowed custom timestamp formatting, potentially causing logs to default to system time zones and reducing forensic precision. Users should review rsyslogd configuration files for timestamp settings and apply any vendor updates that reintroduce desired formatting options.

item.title: VirusTotal Detects Ransomware Missed by 75 AV Engines
item.description: VirusTotal introduced a runtime encryption check that identified a Python ransomware sample previously undetected by 75 antivirus engines. The malware leveraged obfuscated Python code to evade static signatures, but its encryption activity triggered the new behavior analysis, revealing its malicious intent. Security teams should enable VirusTotal’s behavior-based detection and ensure their antivirus solutions are updated to recognize similar obfuscated ransomware.

item.title: Cleverbridge Reports Credit Card Data Theft
item.description: Cleverbridge, an e-commerce platform, disclosed a breach that exposed customers’ payment card numbers and CVV codes via unauthorized system access. The intrusion involved credential theft and data exfiltration, potentially enabling fraud, but no public exploit or CVE was identified. Cleverbridge urged affected users to monitor accounts, change passwords, and contact issuers while investigating the vector and will issue remediation guidance.

item.title: Optimizely Malware Hits 178 Organizations
item.description: An attacker exploited a flaw in Optimizely’s web experimentation platform to plant malicious JavaScript on 178 organizations’ websites, such as BBC, CNN, and Zoom. The vulnerability, a memory-corruption flaw in OpenJDK’s Base64 decoder (CVE-2026-114938), requires specific CPU conditions, limiting exploitation but still high severity. Optimizely confirmed the incident, urged customers to update the platform, remove injected scripts, and monitor traffic.

item.title: OpenRouter Removes Providers After Prompt Theft Discovery
item.description: OpenRouter removed three AI inference providers after researchers uncovered months of prompt theft from their internal systems. The stolen prompts, some marked Zero Data Retention, were accessed without authorization, exposing user inputs; Dragos confirmed the breach to vendors. OpenRouter recommends vendors review access controls, enforce strict data-retention policies, and apply security hardening to prevent future prompt exfiltration.

item.title: Ghostscript Sandbox Escape RCE Demonstrated via File Uploads
item.description: Researchers demonstrated a sandbox-escape RCE flaw in Ghostscript, a common PDF/PostScript interpreter on Linux servers, via crafted file uploads. The flaw lets attackers bypass Ghostscript’s isolation and run arbitrary commands on the host, compromising the web application; a PoC was released by pwn.ai. Ghostscript issued a patch; admins should apply it immediately and verify file-upload handling remains sandboxed.

item.title: OpenRouter Removes Compromised AI Hosts, Revokes Zero Data Retention
item.description: OpenRouter removed three AI hosting providers and revoked Zero Data Retention for 125 endpoints after detecting provider compromise. The flaw arises from third-party providers lacking secure isolation, risking private chat data leakage; no breach confirmed, but exposure persists. OpenRouter notified affected customers, removed compromised providers, and revoked Zero Data Retention; teams should verify endpoint settings and monitor anomalous access.

item.title: Red Hat Issues Critical PHP Patch for RHEL7
item.description: Red Hat released a critical PHP update for RHEL7 Extended Lifecycle Support, fixing high-severity vulnerabilities that could allow remote code execution. The patch covers several CVE-identified flaws, each rated with a CVSS base score indicating critical impact, though no exploitation has been seen. Apply the update immediately via RHSA-2026:101337 to keep PHP secure.

item.title: Ghostscript Upload2Shell Enables Remote Command Execution
item.description: Ghostscript’s Type 1 font loader flaw, CVE-2026-125396, allows attackers to run arbitrary commands on WordPress, Roundcube, and print servers via file processing. The flaw does not need direct Ghostscript exposure, yet it grants remote code execution on any server that processes malicious fonts. Patches for Ghostscript 10.08.0+ are released; administrators should upgrade immediately to eliminate the risk.

item.title: Red Hat Issues Critical PHP 8.2 Update
item.description: Red Hat issued a critical update for php:8.2 on RHEL8, fixing vulnerabilities that could enable remote code execution via PHP scripts. The CVE entries show CVSS scores up to 9.8, allowing unauthenticated attackers to run arbitrary code on affected servers. Administrators should apply the php:8.2 patch immediately and confirm the new module version is deployed to mitigate the risk.

item.title: Entra Connect Health Flaw Exposes Admin Emails
item.description: A flaw in Microsoft Entra Connect Health lets attackers read admin and technical contact email addresses and config data. The vulnerability offers read-only access to these records but no inbox or message retrieval, and was disclosed via a Reddit customer notice. Microsoft applied a fix on November 19; administrators should patch immediately to stop data exposure.

item.title: Rackspace Spot Breach Exposes Customer Kubernetes Secrets
item.description: Hackers breached Rackspace Spot cloud platform using compromised credentials, deploying unauthorized workloads and accessing Kubernetes secrets in customer clusters. The breach leveraged stolen credentials to read sensitive cluster secrets, exposing potential data leakage without exploiting a known software flaw. Rackspace urged customers to rotate compromised credentials, audit workloads, and apply any available platform updates to mitigate the exposure.

item.title: Red Hat Issues Critical Update for PHP 8.2
item.description: Red Hat released a critical security update for the php:8.2 module on RHEL 9.8 Extended Update Support, addressing high-impact vulnerabilities. The flaws, listed in CVE references, enable remote code execution via malformed input, with CVSS scores up to 9.8. Red Hat recommends applying the update immediately; no workaround exists, and users should verify module integrity post-installation.

item.title: Red Hat Issues Critical Update for PHP 8.3
item.description: Red Hat released a critical security update for the php:8.3 module on RHEL 9.8 Extended Update Support, addressing high-impact vulnerabilities. The flaws, listed in CVE references, enable remote code execution via malformed input, with CVSS scores up to 9.8. Red Hat recommends applying the update immediately; no workaround exists, and users should verify module integrity post-installation.

item.title: Microsoft Entra Connect Health Breach Exposes Admin Emails
item.description: Attackers exploited a flaw in Microsoft Entra Connect Health, gaining unauthorized access to administrator email addresses and tenant configuration data. The flaw enabled remote code execution via a malformed authentication token, letting attackers read tenant settings without credentials. Microsoft issued a patch and urged customers to update Entra Connect Health immediately, disabling the affected API endpoint as a temporary mitigation.

item.title: MCP Servers Pose New AI Attack Surface
item.description: MCP lets AI apps connect to external tools, APIs, and business data, making each server a new attack surface. Misconfigurations or weak authentication allow attackers to gain unauthorized access, potentially compromising corporate systems and data. Apply strict access controls, enable MFA, audit settings, and install vendor patches regularly to mitigate risks.

item.title: Red Hat Issues Critical Update for PHP 7.4
item.description: Red Hat released a critical security update for the php:7.4 module on RHEL 8, addressing high-impact vulnerabilities. The flaws, listed in CVE references, enable remote code execution via malformed input, with CVSS scores up to 9.8. Red Hat recommends applying the update immediately; no workaround exists, and users should verify module integrity post-installation.

item.title: FBI NCIC Database Breach Exposes Sensitive Law Enforcement Records
item.description: FBI National Crime Information Center (NCIC) database was breached, exposing case files and personnel records. Attackers exploited an undisclosed flaw to gain unauthorized access, potentially compromising investigative workflows. Investigators are isolating the breach, patching the flaw, urging agencies to review NCIC access controls, and coordinating with federal cybersecurity teams to mitigate further exposure.

item.title: CrowdStrike Negotiates Zscaler Acquisition
item.description: CrowdStrike is negotiating a potential acquisition of Zscaler, the cloud-security platform provider that offers zero-trust networking and secure web gateways. The deal could consolidate market share, expand CrowdStrike's cloud security portfolio, and reshape vendor competition by integrating Zscaler's zero-trust solutions. Both firms are conducting due diligence, and the transaction remains unconfirmed pending regulatory review and shareholder approval.

item.title: Trump Names Kirsten Davies National Cyber Director
item.description: White House appoints Kirsten Davies as National Cyber Director to steer America First cyber strategy and oversee federal cyber operations. Davies brings experience from previous cyber leadership roles, expected to shape national cyber defense priorities and cybersecurity policy coordination. The appointment signals a shift toward a more aggressive cyber posture; stakeholders should monitor policy developments and regulatory initiatives.

item.title: China-Linked Hackers Exploit MONAI Label Zero-Day
item.description: China-linked threat actors used autonomous Cairn AI agents to locate and exploit a critical vulnerability in MONAI Label medical software. The flaw permits unauthenticated critical remote code execution via malformed input, enabling data exfiltration from imaging systems. Amazon issued an out-of-band patch; all MONAI Label users should apply it immediately.

item.title: Malicious Webpage Extracts Meta Muse Private Chats
item.description: Researchers showed a single malicious webpage can extract private conversations and stored memories from Meta Muse without approval prompts. The method could also harvest credentials for connected accounts, but the demo was confined to one user and did not impact real users. Meta has not issued a fix; users should avoid untrusted webpages and consider disabling Muse until further guidance.

item.title: GPGME Memory Bug Exposes App Data via Malicious Keys
item.description: A malicious OpenPGP key with an unusually long user ID triggers a critical memory bug in GPGME, the core library of GnuPG, exposing application data. The flaw, CVE-2026-129975, affects all software using GPGME before 2.3.0 and lets attackers read memory without authentication. GnuPG released patched versions; users should upgrade to GPGME 2.3.0+ and enforce key-length checks to mitigate the issue.

item.title: AI Agents Exploit MONAI Label Zero-Day for Root Access
item.description: AI agents discovered a zero-day in MONAI Label 0.8.5 and earlier, an open-source medical-imaging server, and used it to gain root on a university server. The flaw permits unauthenticated writes outside the server’s storage folder, enabling full system control without credentials. A patch for MONAI Label 0.8.5+ is available; admins should upgrade immediately and restrict default write permissions.

item.title: Signal Blocks AI Screenshot Access on iOS 27 and Android
item.description: Signal announced a new screenshot-blocking feature to prevent AI assistants from capturing private chats on iOS 27 and Android. The update addresses a privacy flaw that allowed screen-data interception, enabling AI agents to harvest message content without user interaction. Users can now install the patch to safeguard conversations, though the protection remains incomplete against advanced AI detection.

item.title: CISA Adds VMware, Cisco, Apache Flaws to KEV
item.description: CISA added four actively exploited flaws to its KEV list, including a CVE-2026-129448 vulnerability in Broadcom VMware vCenter. The CVE-2026-129448 flaw, a deserialization of untrusted data with CVSS 9.8, enables remote code execution across VMware, Cisco Expressway, Apache Roller, and SAP NetWeaver systems. Patches are available for all affected products; administrators must apply updates immediately to mitigate the high-risk exploitation.

item.title: 6 Critical F5 BIG-IP . Could Let Hackers Disrupt Websites and Execute Malicious Code
item.description: F5 released emergency fixes for six critical BIG-IP vulnerabilities that could let remote attackers take websites and other services offline without logging in. The flaws affect specific traffic-handling configurations. An attacker who can reach a vulnerable service could crash the BIG-IP process that handles client traffic.

item.title: WhatsApp Android Flaws Could Let Hackers Delete Users’ Files and Expose IP Addresses
item.description: WhatsApp’s November 2026 security update describes three flaws that could let attackers delete files stored by WhatsApp on Android, expose a user’s IP address, or bypass a security check for Meta AI’s Private Processing service. Of the three, only the IP exposure flaw was flagged for possible abuse.

item.title: Top Enterprise Risk Management Tools 2027
item.description: The 2027 ERM landscape features platforms that enable organizations to identify, assess, and mitigate risks across operational, financial, compliance, and cybersecurity domains. These solutions leverage AI, machine learning, and automation to deliver real-time insights and streamline processes, while prioritizing seamless integration for centralized data views. Vendors emphasize AI-driven analytics and unified dashboards to support holistic risk management.

item.title: CTO of ‘RansomwareHelp’ Indicted for Wire Fraud
item.description: The chief technology officer and co-founder of ransomwarehelp.com, a six year old Florida business that claimed to use "advanced cryptographic tools" to restore data locked by ransomware, has been charged with wire fraud after an FBI sting operation found the company was simply paying the attackers for a decryption key and charging victims a markup for work that was never performed.

item.title: NGINX CVEs Impact Palo Alto Products
item.description: Palo Alto Networks reported that CVE-2026-123633 and CVE-2026-123007, NGINX vulnerabilities, impact its firewall and threat prevention products. These critical flaws enable remote code execution in NGINX, potentially compromising Palo Alto devices and exposing network traffic. Patches addressing both CVEs are available; administrators should update affected systems immediately to prevent exploitation.

item.title: Com Group Conducts Vishing Data Theft Extortion
item.description: Com affiliates execute vishing attacks, cloud data theft, and extortion campaigns targeting healthcare and finance organizations. Attackers leverage voice phishing to harvest credentials, exfiltrate cloud-stored data, and demand ransom payments, resulting in operational disruption and sensitive data exposure. Unit 42 recommends phishing-resistant multi-factor authentication, continuous cloud monitoring, and robust incident response planning to mitigate risks.

item.title: West Virginia Legislature Suffers Cyber Incident
item.description: A cybersecurity incident disrupted West Virginia Legislature IT systems starting Thursday and continued through Friday. The attack vector remains undisclosed, but containment prevented lateral movement to other state government networks. Legislative IT teams are actively restoring systems while investigators assess potential data compromise and implement additional safeguards.

item.title: RHSA-2026:100822: Critical: nginx security update
item.description: An update for nginx is now available for Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9.4 Update Services for SAP Solutions. Red Hat Product Security has rated this update as having a security impact of Critical. A Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) base score, which gives a detailed severity rating, is available for each vulnerability from the CVE link(s) in the References section.

item.title: Red Hat Issues Critical PHP 8.4 Security Update to Fix Remote Code Execution Vulnerabilities
item.description: Red Hat released a critical PHP 8.4 update on RHEL 10, fixing remote code execution flaws triggered by crafted input streams. The patch addresses CVEs with CVSS scores up to 9.8, removing the risk of unauthenticated exploitation. Red Hat urges immediate application of RHSA-2026-100821, with no workarounds, and users to verify PHP 8.4 version to confirm the fix.

item.title: China's 'Armory Castle' Lays Siege to VMware vCenter Zero-Day
item.description: During the last wave of major VMware vCenter security updates, a China-nexus threat group likely already had its next zero-day up its sleeve. The vulnerability is tracked as CVE-2026-123890.

item.title: RHSA-2026:100814: Critical: nginx security update
item.description: An update for nginx is now available for Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9.6 Extended Update Support. Red Hat Product Security has rated this update as having a security impact of Critical. A Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) base score, which gives a detailed severity rating, is available for each vulnerability from the CVE link(s) in the References section.

item.title: House Committee Rebukes Chinese AI Adoption
item.description: The House Homeland Security Committee launched an investigation into U.S. corporate adoption of Chinese open-weight AI models. Lawmakers cite supply chain risks, potential data exfiltration, and intellectual property theft as primary concerns for national security. The committee recommends stricter vetting of AI model provenance and enhanced export controls to mitigate strategic vulnerabilities.

item.title: How Cloudflare WAF protects against ruby2shell (CVE-2026-132825)
item.description: ruby2shell lets attackers corrupt memory in default Rails and Sinatra apps without logging in. Cloudflare WAF blocks it for every customer, including Free plans. Upgrade Ruby now, and use the WAF to cover the gap.

item.title: How Cloudflare WAF helps protect against phpAfterShell and other critical PHP flaws
item.description: phpAfterShell is a critical flaw in PHP's default session handler that can lead to code execution. Cloudflare WAF blocks it for all customers, including Free plans, and adds new rules for other PHP flaws fixed in the same release. The vulnerability is tracked as CVE-2026-126714.

item.description: An update for nginx is now available for Red Hat Enterprise Linux 10.2 Extended Update Support. Red Hat Product Security has rated this update as having a security impact of Critical. A Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) base score, which gives a detailed severity rating, is available for each vulnerability from the CVE link(s) in the References section.

item.title: Cisco Products Hit by Vulnerabilities, CVE Added to KEV
item.description: Cisco products including IOS XR, Expressway, Snort 3, Cyber Vision, Secure FTD, Secure Client, and several collaboration services are affected by multiple vulnerabilities. CISA added CVE-2026-76466 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities database, indicating active exploitation potential for the affected components. Cisco recommends applying the latest firmware and software updates for the listed products immediately to mitigate the risk.

item.title: The Container Store Restores Operations Following Weekend Cyberattack
item.description: The Container Store experienced a weekend cyberattack that impacted its corporate website and internal IT systems. Parent company Neighborhood Intelligence disclosed that the unauthorized security incident temporarily disrupted operational infrastructure across the retail enterprise. The organization has fully restored its website and core systems following remediation efforts to address the cyber disruption.

item.title: SAP releases multi-product security updates
item.description: SAP released a security advisory for SQL Anywhere Monitor, Solution Manager, CommonCryptoLib, HANA JDBC Client, Business Connector, NetWeaver Portal, S/4HANA, HANA 2.0, SAP GUI, and Starter Solution. The patches address memory corruption, authentication bypass, and privilege escalation flaws across 20+ SAP components, with CVE IDs omitted. SAP recommends applying the latest patches for each affected product immediately to prevent exploitation.

item.title: Google Releases Chrome Dev 160 for Android
item.description: Google released Chrome Dev version 160.0.8171.0 for Android via the Google Play store, marking the latest development channel milestone. The update incorporates unspecified security patches and feature enhancements documented in the Chromium git log and official blog posts. Android users should install this release promptly to obtain the latest stability improvements and vulnerability mitigations.

item.title: Arctic Wolf reports record October threat activity
item.description: Arctic Wolf Aurora Incident Response recorded a 78% rise in non-customer cases and a 96% increase in sophisticated network intrusions, including ransomware, in October 2026. The surge indicates attackers are more active and employing advanced tactics, stressing the importance of rapid detection and response. Teams should update incident response plans, deploy automation, and monitor emerging patterns to reduce future risk.

item.title: Bell Canada Breach Exposes Enterprise Customer Data
item.description: Bell Canada confirmed that an 'agentic' threat actor breached its systems on November 17 2026, accessing enterprise customer data. The intrusion exploited vulnerabilities in the order-and-provisioning platform, allowing attackers to exfiltrate sensitive customer records. Bell Canada has issued a public advisory and is coordinating with security teams to apply patches and strengthen authentication controls.
